indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: to muff something is to bungle it, so muffs means botches

explanation.surface: Someone notices marks left on their fur muffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muffs' looks like a plural noun (the fur hand-warmers) but is the verb, to bungle.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotches are irregular marks or patches, the same thing as stains.

indicators.note: short asks for the word to be cut by its final letter

parts.note: spare means frugal or economical

explanation.surface: A brief economic boom is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boom' reads as an economic upturn, but here it is the nautical sense. 'Short' trims the last letter off SPARE.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing ship a boom is a spar, a pole holding the foot of a sail.

clue.text: Cover for house in Thailand with a half-door

parts.note: T is the international vehicle registration code for Thailand
a hatch is a half-door, as in a stable door split across the middle

explanation.surface: A house in Thailand is fitted with a stable-style door.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is straw or reed laid as a roof, the covering on top of a cottage.

parts.note: to tax is to strain or overburden
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone overloads a single vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab for hire is a vehicle.

clue.text: Snickers immoderately about article, showing eccentricity

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the other piece
acting immoderately suggests the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone giggles excessively at a newspaper article, showing an odd streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' wants to be a newspaper piece being laughed at; it is the grammatical article. Snickers is the word itself, not the chocolate bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Crankiness here is the quality of a crank, an oddball, i.e. eccentricity.

clue.text: Cut with tip of short pointed tool

parts.note: a cut is a hairstyle, a style

indicators.note: tip of picks the end letter of the following word, here its last

explanation.surface: Something is cut using the end of a small sharp implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip of short' takes the final letter T of 'short'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylet is a slender probe or stiletto, a small sharp instrument.

clue.text: Chums running round dead tree with no care

indicators.note: running round signals the word turns about so it reads backwards

parts.note: chums are pals
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: Friends jog carelessly around a dead tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running round' is a reversal signal here, not chums jogging about the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done slapdash is done carelessly, hastily and without attention.

clue.text: Quality found in chain mail, for instance?

definitions.text: Quality found in chain mail, for instance?

parts.words: Quality found in chain mail, for instance?
parts.note: the armour reading is a decoy: the words chain and mail share a vowel sound, a feature of poetic sound

explanation.surface: Someone describes a property of medieval armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chain mail' suggests armour, but the point is the two words: they rhyme on their vowel only (ai/ai) without fully rhyming consonants elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Assonance is the repetition of vowel sounds in nearby words, a resemblance of sound in verse.

parts.note: a rate is a count or measured figure

explanation.surface: A European nobleman is stirred up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a nobleman; it means a rate, as in a pulse count.
explanation.definitionFit: To aerate is to charge with gas, so making a liquid fizz or sparkle: to stir up.

indicators.note: around tells us the word turns back on itself

parts.note: rot means decay

explanation.surface: Rot has set in around an American decorative moulding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is a reversal signal, not a container: nothing is put inside anything.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture a torus is a large convex rounded moulding at the base of a column.

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a tangle is a muddle or confusion
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: A government official is a figure in a muddled state.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-sided shape is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Liberal active patron, this (after the Greek character)

definitions.text: Liberal active patron, this (after the Greek character)

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the Greek letter in the answer

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: active suggests the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A generous patron is described, with a nod to Greek lettering.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a liberal, active patron. The bracket tells you the Greek letter comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactor who gives generously to good causes is a liberal patron of them.

parts.note: marriage lines is a wedding certificate; here read as lines of verse written about romance and wedlock

explanation.walkthrough: 'Marriage lines' is a British phrase for a marriage certificate; the clue reinterprets lines as verses about love.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse about romance is poetry whose lines celebrate courtship and marriage.

clue.text: You could make jam with this

definitions.text: You could make jam with this

parts.words: You could make jam with this
parts.note: jam suggests fruit preserve, but it means a crush of people or traffic, caused by packing in too many

explanation.walkthrough: 'jam' wants to be the fruit spread; it is a congested crush.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack too many people into a space creates a jam, a crush or congestion.

indicators.note: after puts the first-named piece behind the second-named one

parts.note: evens means makes level, equalises

explanation.surface: A team levels the score moments after falling behind in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Sevens is short-form rugby union played with seven a side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is a sport, a seven-a-side version of rugby.

definitions.meaning: spartan means austere, harsh and plain

explanation.surface: A Spartan warrior's burial place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spartan's grave' looks like a burial site; it is two adjectives joined by a link 's.
explanation.definitionFit: Both austere and serious describe something harsh or stern.

indicators.note: about places the rearranged letters round the other piece
affected means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six

explanation.surface: A notice to quit affects six tenants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' looks like describing the notice's effect but is the anagram signal; the surface's notice to quit is also the scene of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being turned out of one's home is the expulsion of a tenant, a dispossession.

parts.note: securing craft suggests mooring a boat, but it means acquiring a skilled trade through training

explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' wants to be a vessel (and the answer ends in SHIP), but it is a skill or trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Training under a master is how one gains a skilled trade.

definitions.meaning: a suit is a lawsuit, a legal proceeding
a fray is a fight or battle

explanation.walkthrough: 'suit fray' suggests worn clothing; both words mean the same thing in other senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal case brought in court and combat in battle are both called by the same word.

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: an issue is an outflow, something going out

explanation.surface: A television network's first show goes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue can mean a web or interwoven network, as in a tissue of lies.

parts.note: locks of hair are tresses

explanation.surface: Armed forces have regulation haircuts.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics stresses are forces acting on a body; to stress also means to emphasise.

indicators.note: spoken says we want the word as it is said, not written

parts.note: a steppe is a vast grassy plain

explanation.surface: Plain speech is part of the process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain spoken' looks like the adjective plain-spoken; it is a noun, the steppe, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is one stage in a process or procedure.

parts.note: over means ended or finished

explanation.surface: A ship's manifest is completed on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and evident, plainly visible.

indicators.note: lopped means cut off at the head, removing the opening letter

parts.note: to pine is to yearn

explanation.surface: Someone clears a pine tree with its branches lopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like the tree but is the verb, to long.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear money is to net it as profit, to make it.

parts.note: starter can be a first dish of a meal; Epsom is a famous racing venue, so its starter is a pun

explanation.walkthrough: Epsom Downs is an English racecourse, home of the Derby; a starter is also a dish served first.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter is the first dish of a meal, and Epsom is a racing venue of this kind.

indicators.note: poorly signals the letters are put together badly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone poorly prepared is expected to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: The competitor not expected to win is the outsider in a contest.
